title: Letter to Assessors 2026/002 — 2026-27 California Consumer Price Index (inflation factor table 1976-77 to 2026-27)

verified.claim: Base year values rise each year by the California CPI change, capped at 2%.
verified.quote: Revenue and Taxation Code section 51 provides that base year values determined under section 110.1 shall be compounded annually by an inflation factor, not to exceed 2 percent.
Accordingly, please prepare your 2026 assessment roll using an inflation factor of 1.02.

verified.claim: The factor was below 2% in 11 of the 51 roll years listed (for example 2010-11: 0.99763; 2014-15: 1.00454; 2016-17: 1.01525; 2021-22: 1.01036).

title: Change in Ownership — Frequently Asked Questions

verified.claim: An inheritance or a transfer through a trust is a change in ownership.
verified.quote: A transfer can be a sale or purchase, but it also can be a gift or inheritance. Transfers that constitute a change in ownership may occur by any means, including ... transfers by grant, gift, devise, inheritance, trust

verified.claim: On a change in ownership the assessor resets the value to market value as of that date.
verified.quote: Once the county assessor has determined that a change in ownership has occurred, Proposition 13 requires the county assessor to reassess the property to its current fair market value as of the date ownership changed.

verified.claim: The homeowners' exemption removes $7,000 of taxable value for an owner-occupied principal residence on January 1; it is claimed once on form BOE-266.
verified.quote: The California Constitution provides a $7,000 reduction in the taxable value for a qualifying owner-occupied home. The home must have been the principal place of residence of the owner on the lien date, January 1st. ... The claim form, BOE-266, Claim for Homeowners' Property Tax Exemption, is available from the county assessor.

title: Death of a Real Property Owner — Reporting Requirements

verified.claim: Form BOE-502-D must be filed with the assessor within 150 days of the date of death, including for property held in a trust.
verified.quote: BOE-502-D must be completed for each parcel of real property owned by the decedent at the time of death to report to the Assessor the transfer of property, including a transfer through the medium of a trust. ... File BOE-502-D, Change in Ownership Statement—Death of a Real Property Owner within 150 days after the date of death.

agency: City and County of San Francisco, Treasurer & Tax Collector
title: Secured Property Taxes

verified.quote: The secured property tax rate for Fiscal Year 2026-27 is 1.18162182%.

verified.claim: The bill is taxable value times the rate, plus direct charges and special assessments.
verified.quote: Total Due (Net Assessed Taxable Value * Tax Rate = Total Tax) + (Total Direct Charges and Special Assessments).

title: Revenue and Taxation Code § 11911 — Documentary transfer tax

verified.claim: The county documentary transfer tax on a sale is $0.55 per $500 of value ($1.10 per $1,000, or 0.11%).
